operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 13261 of March 19, 2002 (67 FR 13243), section 4(d), replaced section 3(a) of Executive Order 13244. Before: the held 2001 text of section 3(a) says that no individual serving in an office listed in section 2(a)-(f) in an acting capacity shall act as Secretary pursuant to this Executive Order. After: the replacement text keeps the same offices, section 2(a)-(f), and the same bar but adds the words that no such individual shall act as Secretary by virtue of so serving, and refers to this order instead of this Executive Order. Under the strike-and-insert ruling (2026-10-21) the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends, and the amendment is a later event with its own date; the substance changed in a limited way (it clarifies that the bar applies to service by virtue of the acting office). The 13261 amendment is on signing (March 19, 2002; Federal Register issue of March 21, 2002). This clause is the heading of section 3, Exceptions, and the whole of section 3(a), the bar on an individual serving in an acting capacity in an office listed in section 2(a)-(f) from acting as Secretary under the order. Executive Order 13915 of April 14, 2020 (85 FR 21733, April 17, 2020), section 4, says Executive Order 13244 of December 18, 2001 (Providing an Order of Succession Within the Department of the Interior) is hereby revoked. Presidential Documents
66267
Federal Register
Vol. 66, No. 246
Friday, December 21, 2001
Title 3—
The President
Executive Order 13244 of December 18, 2001
Providing an Order of Succession Within the Department of
the Interior
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the
laws of the United States of America, including Subchapter III of Chapter
33 of title 5 of the United States Code, it is hereby ordered that:
Section 1. Subject to the provisions of section 3 of this Executive Order,
the officers named in section 2, in the order listed, shall act as and perform
the functions and duties of the office of Secretary of the Interior (Secretary)
during any period when both the Secretary and the Deputy Secretary of
the Interior (Deputy Secretary) have died, resigned, or are otherwise unable
to perform the functions and duties of the office of Secretary.
Sec. 2. Order of Succession.
(a) Solicitor of the Department of the Interior;
(b) Assistant Secretary of the Interior in charge of Policy, Management
and Budget;
(c) Assistant Secretary of the Interior in charge of Land and Minerals
Management;
(d) Assistant Secretary of the Interior in charge of Water and Science;
(e) Assistant Secretary of the Interior for Fish and Wildlife and Parks;
and
(f) Assistant Secretary of the Interior for Indian Affairs.
Sec. 3. Exceptions.
(a) No individual who is serving in an office listed in section 2(a)–
(f) in an acting capacity shall act as Secretary pursuant to this Executive
Order.
(b) Notwithstanding the provisions of this Executive Order, the President
retains discretion, to the extent permitted by Subchapter III of Chapter
33 of title 5 of the United States Code, to depart from this Executive
Order in designating an acting Secretary.
Sec. 4. Executive Order 11487 of October 6, 1969, is hereby revoked.
W
THE WHITE HOUSE,
December 18, 2001.
[FR Doc. 01–31669
Filed 12–20–01; 8:45 am]

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 4 revokes Executive Order 11487 of October 6, 1969. A revocation is complete when made and nothing in the order defers it, so this clause was performed on signing, December 18, 2001 (the order was filed December 20, 2001 and published December 21, 2001, 66 FR 66267). The first end is therefore performance on issue, earlier than the revocation of the whole order in 2020; the order's own end (April 14, 2020) is the latest first end among the clauses and is the whole-order end.

research_rationale:
EO 13244 (Providing an Order of Succession Within the Department of the Interior; 66 FR 66267, December 21, 2001) was read in full from the held Federal Register original. It sets a standing order of succession for the Secretary of the Interior. It was amended once (EO 13261, March 19, 2002, section 3(a) only) and was expressly revoked in its entirety by section 4 of EO 13915 (April 14, 2020; 85 FR 21733), whose text is held; EO 13915 then re-issues a similar succession order of its own. No held source shows an earlier end. The catalog note (Revokes: EO 11487; Amended by: EO 13261; Revoked by: EO 13915), the held 5 U.S.C. 3345 note and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register catalog and saved order texts) agree. The status decision records 'no': the order was formally revoked and has no operative force on 2026-10-14.

Presidential Documents
21733 
Federal Register 
Vol. 85, No. 75 
Friday, April 17, 2020 
Title 3— 
The President 
Executive Order 13915 of April 14, 2020 
Providing an Order of Succession Within the Department of 
the Interior 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including the Federal Vacancies Reform 
Act of 1998, 5 U.S.C. 3345 et seq., it is hereby ordered that: 
Section 1. Subject to the provisions of section 3 of this order, the officers 
named in section 2, in the order listed, shall act as and perform the functions 
and duties of the office of Secretary of the Interior (Secretary) during any 
period when both the Secretary and the Deputy Secretary of the Interior 
have died, resigned, or are otherwise unable to perform the functions and 
duties of the office of Secretary. 
Sec. 2. Order of Succession. (a) Solicitor of the Department of the Interior; 
(b) Assistant Secretary of the Interior in charge of Policy, Management, 
and Budget; 
(c) Assistant Secretary of the Interior in charge of Land and Minerals 
Management; 
(d) Assistant Secretary of the Interior in charge of Water and Science; 
(e) Assistant Secretary of the Interior for Fish and Wildlife; 
(f) Assistant Secretary of the Interior in charge of Indian Affairs; and 
(g) Assistant Secretary of the Interior in charge of Insular and International 
Affairs. 
Sec. 3. Exceptions. (a) No individual who is serving in an office listed 
in section 2 of this order in an acting capacity shall, by virtue of so serving, 
act as Secretary pursuant to this order. 
(b) Notwithstanding the provisions of this order, the President retains 
discretion, to the extent permitted by the Federal Vacancies Reform Act 
of 1998, to depart from this order in designating an acting Secretary.
